See the related Topic “Book of Commandments.”

For example, see “Revelation, circa Early 1830,” in Revelation Book 1, 30–31,josephsmithpapers.org; “Revelation, 15 May 1831,” in Revelation Book 1, 85,josephsmithpapers.org; “Revelation, 20 March 1832,” in Revelation Book 1, 148,josephsmithpapers.org; “Revelation, 28 April 1834,” in Revelation Book 1, 198,josephsmithpapers.org.

On the documented visions of Joseph Smith, see Alexander L. Baugh, “Parting the Veil: Joseph Smith’s Seventy-six Documented Visionary Experiences,” in John W. Welch, ed.,Opening the Heavens: Accounts of Divine Manifestations, 1820–1844(Provo, Utah: Brigham Young University Press, 2005), 265–326. On two occasions, Joseph Smith wrote prayers under revelatory inspiration (see “Revelation, 30 October 1831 [D&C 65],” in Revelation Book 1, 112,josephsmithpapers.org; “Prayer of Dedication, 27 March 1836 [D&C 109],”josephsmithpapers.org). On Joseph Smith’s inspired translations, see related Topics “Joseph Smith Translation of the Bible,” “Book of Mormon Translation,” and “Book of Abraham Translation.” Joseph Smith also translated a lost parchment of the ancient disciple John (see “Account of John, April 1829–C [D&C 7],” in Revelation Book 1, 13–14,josephsmithpapers.org).
